name: Slopcheck

status.note: Written over five days in March 2026; no commits since March 19, 2026.

summary: A small Rust CLI that reports signs of AI-assisted development in a repository and its Rust or JavaScript dependencies: commits by known coding agents and files such as `CLAUDE.md` or `.cursor`.
intro: Slopcheck is a personal project, and it is not a linter in the usual sense: it reads no code and reports no style or correctness problems. It answers one question, how much a project and everything it depends on was built with AI coding tools. In a Git repository it walks the history and counts commits whose author, or whose `Co-authored-by:` trailer, is a known agent address (Claude, Copilot, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Jules, Junie, Qwen, GLM and review bots such as CodeRabbit and Greptile), separately for all time and the past 30 days, so it can tell current from former use. It also looks for agent files such as `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.mcp.json`, `.cursor` or `.clinerules` in the working tree, and in `.gitignore` for projects that hide them.

It then lists dependencies, with `cargo metadata` for Rust or by naively parsing `package.json` and walking npm for JavaScript, clones each dependency’s repository (metadata only, cached for 24 hours under `~/.cache/slopcheck`) and runs the same checks, assuming each is on its latest version. Install it with `cargo install --git https://github.com/mat-1/slopcheck` and run `slopcheck ./project`. The README warns against running it on untrusted projects, because it may fetch arbitrary sources and run build scripts.
strengths: Shows at a glance which dependencies are developed with AI coding agents, for teams with a policy on that
Uses plain, checkable signals (commit metadata and config files) rather than guessing from the code’s style
limits: Only finds what is declared: agent work committed under a human’s name with no trailer or config file is invisible
Only Rust and npm dependencies, checked at their latest version rather than the one you lock
May run build scripts of the projects it inspects, so it is unsafe on untrusted code
A personal project with no licence file and no releases (install from Git), dormant since March 2026

story: The developer mat (GitHub user mat-1) wrote Slopcheck in a burst between March 14 and 19, 2026: the first version checked Rust projects for agent commits and files, contributors and later commits added more agents and review bots, and JavaScript support arrived on March 16. It has not changed since.

choices.choice: Look at provenance, not at the code
choices.why: Commit authors, co-author trailers and agent config files are explicit records the tools leave behind, which a small program can count without judging the code itself.
A project’s own history says little if the libraries it pulls in are written by agents, so it clones and checks each dependency’s repository too.
